questions.q: How old was Jotham when he became king of Judah and how long did he reign?
questions.a: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem.

questions.q: How did the people of Judah behave even though Jotham did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh?
questions.a: The people of Judah still behaved in evil ways, even though Jotham did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Jotham build in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Jotham built the upper gate of the house of Yahweh, and he built much on the hill of Ophel.

questions.q: What did Jotham build in the hill country and forests of Judah?
questions.a: Jotham built cities in the hill country, and castles and towers in the forests of Judah.

questions.q: Why did the people of Ammon give Jotham silver, wheat, and barley?
questions.a: The people of Ammon gave Jotham silver, wheat, and barley because he fought with them and defeated them.
Jotham became powerful because he walked firmly before Yahweh his God.

questions.q: Where was Jotham buried when he died?
questions.a: Jotham was buried in the city of David.

questions.q: Who became king of Judah after the death of Jotham?
questions.a: Ahaz, Jotham’s son, became king in his place.

commentary.text: —The people did corruptly. Perhaps Jotham was wanting towards the reformation of the land. Men may be very good, and yet not have courage and zeal to do what they might. It certainly casts blame upon the people. Jotham prospered, and became mighty. The more stedfast we are in religion, the more mighty we are, both to resist evil, and to do good. The Lord often removes wise and pious rulers, and sends others, whose follies and vices punish a people that valued not their mercies.
